summary: Inspected the supplied RDKit Recap.py source and BSD-3-Clause license. RECAP terminal fragment retrieval is well-scoped as a reusable skill: a sanitized RDKit Mol is decomposed with the documented predefined bond-cleavage SMARTS; root.children, GetAllChildren(), and GetLeaves() have distinct meanings, and valid empty leaf sets are common for chains, rings, and protonated/charged forms. One candidate packages terminal leaf retrieval with input validation and boundary notes.

candidates.name: rdkit-recap-terminal-fragments
candidates.capability: Decompose a sanitized RDKit molecule into RECAP terminal fragments using rdkit.Chem.Recap.RecapDecompose and root.GetLeaves(), returning terminal leaf fragments keyed by canonical SMILES with attachment points represented as '*' atoms.
candidates.boundary: Input is an RDKit Mol from a valid, parseable SMILES/source; invalid SMILES returning None is out of scope and callers must validate before calling. Output is the standard terminal fragment dictionary (SMILES -> RecapHierarchyNode); intermediate/full hierarchy via root.children or root.GetAllChildren() is available but is not the primary terminal-fragment result. A valid empty leaf dictionary is expected for molecules with no permitted cleavable bond, rings only, or disallowed charged/protonated forms, not an error.
candidates.value: Removes confusion between immediate children, full descendants, and terminal leaves by documenting that GetLeaves() returns only leaf nodes keyed by canonical product SMILES. It covers dummy '*' labels, canonical keys, default small-fragment rejection, and minFragmentSize/onlyUseReactions controls, so users can obtain standard RECAP terminal fragments without reading RDKit source code or misinterpreting hierarchy nodes as terminal fragments.
candidates.usage_path: from rdkit import Chem; from rdkit.Chem import Recap; mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles); root = Recap.RecapDecompose(mol); leaves = root.GetLeaves()  # dict SMILES -> RecapHierarchyNode; use leaves.keys() for fragment SMILES. Optional controls: RecapDecompose(mol, minFragmentSize=N, onlyUseReactions={...})
candidates.construction: Direct packaging of the documented rdkit.Chem.Recap API from the provided source; no new algorithm or research extension. Delivery would include a SKILL.md focused on terminal-fragment retrieval plus examples extracted from the embedded unit-test cases (e.g., 'C1CC1Oc1ccccc1-c1ncc(OC)cc1' yields three leaves; 'CCCOCCC' yields an empty default leaf dict; 'CCCOCCC' with minFragmentSize=3 yields one leaf), BSD-3-Clause attribution, and a compatible RDKit environment prerequisite. No runtime package is authored at this discovery stage.

evidence.claim: RecapDecompose(mol, allNodes=None, minFragmentSize=0, onlyUseReactions=None) returns a RecapHierarchyNode and uses canonical MolToSmiles(mol,1) as its registry key; it recursively runs the predefined reactionDefs SMARTS reactions and stores fragment nodes keyed by product SMILES.
GetLeaves() returns a dictionary keyed by SMILES of leaf (terminal) nodes, descending recursively only into non-terminal children via _gacRecurse(res, terminalOnly=True).

The predefined reactionDefs tuple defines 12 bond-cleavage SMARTS including urea, amide, ester, amines, cyclic amines, ether, olefin, aromatic N-aliphatic C, lactam N-aliphatic C, aromatic C-aromatic C, aromatic N-aromatic C (noted as not part of the standard RECAP set), and sulphonamide.

With minFragmentSize=0 (default), the code rejects products whose dummy-stripped SMILES string equals '', 'C', 'CC', or 'CCC' via pSmi.replace('*','').replace('()',''); when minFragmentSize>0, it rejects products where explicit atom count minus '*' dummy count is below minFragmentSize.

Embedded unittests demonstrate valid empty leaves for non-cleavable/ring/protonated cases (e.g., 'CCCOCCC' default, 'C1CCCCO1', 'c1ccccc1[n+]1ccccc1', 'C1CC1[NH+]C(=O)CC') and canonical leaf examples such as 'C1CC1Oc1ccccc1-c1ncc(OC)cc1' producing three leaves.

The retrieved RDKit license is BSD 3-Clause (copyright 2006-2015 Rational Discovery LLC, Greg Landrum, Julie Penzotti and others), permitting redistribution with copyright notice, conditions, and disclaimer.
